posts.title: Cincy Oppo Rally and HW 6HR Enduro
posts.description: What a FUN (read pain) filled weekend! Saturday was our second attempt on Oppo Rally by Arch Duke Maxyenko. If you don’t know about Oppo Rally, it is a huge scale scavenger hunt. it was titled “Oppo Rally Cincinnati 2026, Battle of Ohio”. but of course, it starts in Kentucky. lol. At Devou Park, over looking the skyline of the Cincinnati in slightly hazed air we received this year’s checkpoint list. The list is long and it is physically impossible to visit all the locations. Each locations have points (generally farther away, higher the points), and the checkpoints locations are separated in to categories, and completing all locations in the category will earn extra points. We went over the list, had a general idea of which categories we want to complete, and hit the road. My sponsor, SWMBO is the navigator/route planner/ puzzle solver, while I just enjoy driving the beautiful country road of Ohio. posts.title: Mid-Ohio with CincySCCA
posts.description: What an eventful weekend! CincySCCA hosted their annual Mid-Ohio weekends. TimeTrial / Track Event on Friday, and Races on Sat/Sunday. I had a great fun on Friday in my Spoon – 99 Miata for TT, and had one heat in Track Event testing out Chase’s Spec Miata. The main dish for the weekend came on Saturday Club Race Experience (CRE). This was my first wheel to wheel racing (ish) experience! I’ve participated numerous Track days and Time Trials, but never had an open passing, wheel to wheel event. CRE opens door for ones without a competition license, to get the taste of a racing. I really cannot thank enough to my friend Chase for letting me borrow pretty much everything except for his underwear for this event! From the Nomex socks, racing suites, cool shirts, helmet (with comm setup), and most importantly Sandy, his Spec Miata. posts.title: Watermelon Survived. AGAIN!
posts.description: Great fun courses, hot weather, reliable Watermelon and a super fast co-driver. I got a smidge closer to my co-driver in the afternoon runs, but he is basically an alien so I’ll never catch him… However, considering that he was gaping me by 2 seconds each run in the morning, getting down to within 0.4 sec in the afternoon was a great improvement for me. The $20 shocks were definitely the best value upgrade from the completely busted OEM shocks. Also, you don’t see a car that has the suspension that louder than the exhaust. The squeak, click crack, bang and pop are well orchestrated music of this hard working car…
